title: Graded piece of the sum of a base ideal and a nilpotent ideal with free lower quotients
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subseteq D$ an ideal, $B$ a commutative $D$-algebra, $Q\subseteq B$ an ideal, and $N\ge1$ an integer with $Q^{N+1}=0$. Suppose that, for each $0\le j<N$, the $D$-module $Q^j/Q^{j+1}$ is free of finite rank $r_j$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], where $Q^0=B$. Put $M=Q^N$ and $\mathfrak b=Q+\mathfrak pB$, with $\mathfrak pB$ the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak p$. There exists an isomorphism of $D/\mathfrak p$-modules
$$\mathfrak b^N/\mathfrak b^{N+1}\ \cong\ M/\mathfrak pM\ \oplus\ \bigoplus_{j=0}^{N-1}\left(\mathfrak p^{N-j}/\mathfrak p^{N-j+1}\right)^{\oplus r_j}.$$
Here $\mathfrak pM$ denotes finite sums of multiples $am$, $a\in\mathfrak p$, $m\in M$; the superscript $\oplus r_j$ means a direct sum of $r_j$ copies. No freeness assumption is imposed on $M$, and no reducedness, localness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on either ring.

This isolates the calculation in steps 7--8 of the accepted agent proof of lem-trf-bennett-normal-flat-numerical-criterion, which applies without reducedness. proof.text: For each $0\le j<N$, choose a basis $(\bar e_{j,t})_{1\le t\le r_j}$ of $Q^j/Q^{j+1}$ and representatives $e_{j,t}\in Q^j$. Let $E_j=\sum_tDe_{j,t}\subseteq Q^j$. By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], projecting a relation $\sum_ta_te_{j,t}=0$ to the quotient forces every $a_t=0$; the same argument shows $E_j\cap Q^{j+1}=0$. Subtracting the lifted basis expansion of any $x\bmod Q^{j+1}$ from $x\in Q^j$ proves $Q^j=E_j\oplus Q^{j+1}$, with $E_j\simeq D^{r_j}$. These are module decompositions, not algebra decompositions.

proof.text: Descending induction gives, inside one fixed decomposition of $B$, $$Q^a=M\oplus\bigoplus_{a\le j<N}E_j\quad(0\le a\le N).$$ At $a=N$ this is $Q^N=M$. Given the formula for $a+1$, substitute it into $Q^a=E_a\oplus Q^{a+1}$ from step 1; directness is retained because the second summand contains all the later summands. At $a=0$ we obtain $B=M\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}E_j$.

proof.text: For a $D$-submodule $L\subseteq B$ write $\mathfrak p^eL$ for finite sums of scalar multiples $ax$, with $a\in\mathfrak p^e$, $x\in L$, and put $\mathfrak p^0=D$. For every $a,e\ge0$, $$(\mathfrak pB)^eQ^a=\mathfrak p^eQ^a.$$ Indeed, expand each element of the left side as a sum of products $(u_1b_1)\cdots(u_eb_e)x$; the product $u_1\cdots u_e$ lies in $\mathfrak p^e$ and $b_1\cdots b_ex\in Q^a$. Conversely, express an element of $\mathfrak p^e$ as a finite sum of products of $e$ elements of $\mathfrak p$ and use those products in the left side. For $e=0$, both sides are $Q^a$.

proof.text: Distributivity of ideal multiplication gives $$\mathfrak b^q=\sum_{a=0}^q\mathfrak p^{q-a}Q^a\quad(q\ge0).$$ Here is the induction: at $q=0$ both sides are $B$; multiplying the formula by $Q+\mathfrak pB$ gives the terms $\mathfrak p^{q-a}Q^{a+1}$ and $\mathfrak p^{q+1-a}Q^a$, by step 3. Together their indices cover $0,\ldots,q+1$, and the repeated middle terms do not change an ideal sum. Since $Q^{N+1}=0$, all terms with $a>N$ vanish, so the upper index can be replaced by $\min(q,N)$.

proof.text: Insert step 2 into the formula of step 4. Scalar multiplication distributes across a finite internal direct sum: each scalar multiple is a sum of its coordinate multiples, and each coordinate multiple is itself obtained from that summand. On $M$, the contributions are $\mathfrak p^{q-a}M$ for $0\le a\le\min(q,N)$; on $E_j$, they are $\mathfrak p^{q-a}E_j$ for $0\le a\le\min(q,j)$. Since $\mathfrak p^{e+1}L\subseteq\mathfrak p^eL$, these sums equal their terms of smallest exponent. Thus, as actual submodules of the fixed decomposition of $B$, $$\mathfrak b^q=\mathfrak p^{\max(q-N,0)}M\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}\mathfrak p^{\max(q-j,0)}E_j.$$ No multiplication-compatibility of the chosen $E_j$ is used.

proof.text: At $q=N,N+1$, step 5 reads $$\mathfrak b^N=M\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}\mathfrak p^{N-j}E_j,\qquad \mathfrak b^{N+1}=\mathfrak pM\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}\mathfrak p^{N-j+1}E_j.$$ The coordinate quotient map sends $m+\sum_jx_j$ to $(m\bmod\mathfrak pM,(x_j\bmod\mathfrak p^{N-j+1}E_j)_j)$. It is $D$-linear and surjective by choosing representatives in each of the finitely many coordinates; its kernel is exactly the displayed expression for $\mathfrak b^{N+1}$. Consequently it induces a bijective $D$-linear map from $\mathfrak b^N/\mathfrak b^{N+1}$ onto $M/\mathfrak pM\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}(\mathfrak p^{N-j}E_j/\mathfrak p^{N-j+1}E_j)$.

proof.text: In the basis of $E_j$ chosen in step 1, $\mathfrak p^eE_j$ consists exactly of the vectors whose $r_j$ coefficients lie in $\mathfrak p^e$. Taking each coefficient modulo $\mathfrak p^{e+1}$ therefore gives a bijective $D$-linear map $$\mathfrak p^eE_j/\mathfrak p^{e+1}E_j\simeq(\mathfrak p^e/\mathfrak p^{e+1})^{\oplus r_j}.$$ Set $e=N-j$ in step 6 to obtain the stated formula. The ideal $\mathfrak p$ annihilates both sides: on the left $\mathfrak p\mathfrak b^N\subseteq\mathfrak b^{N+1}$, and on the right this follows from the denominators. The isomorphism is thus $D/\mathfrak p$-linear. The construction never chooses a basis of $M$.

This is a first split of an unsplit node that Q22 created for lem-per-bennett-normal-flat-local-criterion; it is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and there are no new nodes. The only citation is def-weil-pbc-free-module (basis = unique finite coordinates), which is exactly what steps 1 and 7 use. Step 1: lifted bases give Q^j=E_j⊕Q^{j+1}, because projecting a relation kills its coefficients. Step 2: descending induction, with base and inductive step both stated. Step 3: (pB)^eQ^a=p^eQ^a, both inclusions, e=0 included. Step 4: b^q=Σp^{q-a}Q^a by induction. Step 5: coordinatewise minimal exponents max(q-N,0) on M and max(q-j,0) on E_j; I rechecked the index ranges, and the E_j are never multiplied, so they need not be closed under multiplication. Step 6: coordinate quotient with kernel b^{N+1}. Step 7: p^eD^r=(p^e)^r, and p kills both sides, so the map is D/p-linear. The statement matches the parent's use in its step (dimensions over D/p, M not assumed free), and it isolates steps 7-8 of lem-trf-bennett-normal-flat-numerical-criterion without citing that node, so there is no cycle. Small cases: Q=0, p=0, p=D, and D=Z, B=Z[x]/(x^2,2x), Q=(x), p=(2), where M=Z/2 is not free and both sides are (Z/2)^2.
